What Is Vetspire?

Vetspire is an innovative pims for clinical decision-making that was founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Francisco, CA. Unlike most PIMS that started as general practice tools, Vetspire was originally designed for teaching hospitals and specialty clinics, which gives it a unique depth of clinical functionality that general-purpose competitors often lack.

The platform is fully cloud-based and supports small animal, specialty, emergency, teaching hospital environments. We were particularly impressed by its clinical decision support capabilities and its powerful templating system, which allows practices to standardize care protocols while maintaining flexibility for individual cases. Vetspire's interface is notably fast, a detail that matters when clinicians are moving between patients throughout the day.

Vetspire starts at $349/mo on a per full-time veterinarian/month basis. This places it at the premium end of the market, but the depth of clinical tooling and analytics justifies the investment for practices that need that level of sophistication.

Key Features

We evaluated every major feature of Vetspire. Here is a breakdown of what the platform offers.

Clinical decision support

Built-in clinical guidance that helps veterinarians follow best-practice protocols during patient encounters.

EMR templates

A powerful templating engine that lets practices create standardized medical record templates for common procedures and conditions.

Advanced analytics

Deep data analysis tools covering clinical outcomes, revenue per procedure, doctor productivity, and practice-wide performance metrics.

Appointment scheduling

Multi-provider scheduling with support for complex appointment types common in specialty and emergency settings.

Custom workflows

Design workflows for referrals, admissions, discharges, and other multi-step clinical processes.

Charge capture

Automatic charge capture linked to clinical actions, reducing missed billing for procedures and treatments.

Referral management

Tools for managing incoming and outgoing referrals, a critical feature for specialty and teaching hospital environments.

Who Should Look Elsewhere?

No software is perfect for every practice. Here are situations where Vetspire may not be the best fit.

  • Small general practices or start-ups that need a simple, affordable system will find Vetspire to be overkill. Its feature depth and price point are designed for practices with more complex clinical needs.
  • Practices that want a strong client-facing mobile app for pet owners should note that Vetspire does not offer a dedicated pet parent app, unlike competitors such as Digitail.
  • Solo veterinarians who primarily need scheduling, basic records, and invoicing would be better served by Shepherd or Hippo Manager at a fraction of the cost.

Final Verdict

Vetspire is our top pick for specialty clinics, teaching hospitals, and data-driven practices that need clinical decision support and advanced analytics beyond what general-purpose PIMS can offer. At $349/mo it is a premium investment, but the depth of clinical tooling makes it worthwhile for practices operating at a higher level of complexity.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Vetspire cloud-based?
Yes. Vetspire is a cloud-based platform. You can access it from any device with a web browser and an internet connection. There is no server hardware to purchase or maintain.
Does Vetspire offer a free trial?
No, Vetspire does not currently offer a free trial. However, you can contact their sales team to request a personalized demo to see the platform in action before making a decision.
What is Vetspire's starting price?
Vetspire starts at $349 per month. The pricing model is per full-time veterinarian/month, so your actual cost may vary depending on your practice size and configuration. Contact Vetspire directly for an exact quote tailored to your needs.
Is Vetspire good for small practices?
Vetspire can work for small practices, but it is primarily designed for specialty clinics. Smaller practices may find that they are paying for features they do not need. We recommend evaluating alternatives like Shepherd ($99/mo) or Hippo Manager ($120/mo) if you run a small or solo practice.
